metric-envelope.physicalInvariant: The selected machinery must produce and regulate a protected metric-compression envelope; Ar'nock biological embodiment cannot replace metric geometry, horizon, closure, or recovery requirements.
machinery: vascularly supplied distributed field-bearing tissues around the certified envelope boundary
cultivated neural sector controllers with local isolation
mineralized or conductive biological structures acting as mechanism-compatible field formers
regenerative recovery organs and thermal/chemical sinks
metric-envelope.power: Conditioned vessel energy is translated through electrochemical or cultivated conversion stages; gross power is insufficient without field-tissue health, sectional coherence, cooling, and protected unwind reserve.
metric-envelope.navigation: Family-required gravimetry, curvature estimation, route forecasting, and safety-horizon sensing are interpreted through cultivated computation and vibration/acoustic operator interfaces.
metric-envelope.control: Distributed ganglia continuously balance envelope sectors; damaged or diseased regions are isolated before asymmetry consumes structural or unwind margin.
metric-envelope.maintenance: Map tissue conductivity, vascular supply, field-sector phase response, scar burden, controller coherence, and envelope coverage before recertification.
metric-envelope.signature: Metric/gravitational and emergence signatures remain primary; derived Ar'nock additions include metabolic loading, heat, chemistry shifts, vascular activity, and synchronization vibration.
metric-envelope.failure: Family hazards such as envelope asymmetry, horizon/closure instability, or curvature mis-solution combine with occlusion, necrosis, neural desynchronization, tissue tearing, contamination, or regeneration exhaustion.
metric-envelope.infrastructure: No Ar'nock-specific metric corridor, beacon, depot, or calibration network is confirmed; scenario infrastructure must retain its own provenance.
metric-envelope.scaling: Larger protected volumes require more independently controlled biological field sectors, longer coordination paths, increased vascular/cooling capacity, and stronger regional isolation rather than one enlarged organ.
manualProcedure: verify complete living field coverage of the current hull and appendage geometry
compare local ganglion timing against independent gravimetric references
reserve biological and mechanism-specific unwind capacity before spool
abort before commit if any field sector cannot be isolated without violating envelope continuity

gravitic-plane.physicalInvariant: The drive must couple the vessel to usable gravitational/shear terrain and survive branch, gradient, and tidal conditions; biological control style cannot turn gravity terrain into an unconstrained lane.
machinery: distributed gravitic coupling organs tied into structural load paths
long-baseline sensory tissues and cultivated gravimetric processors
sectional recoupling structures with independent vascular supply
branch-voting ganglia and emergency decoupling tissue
gravitic-plane.power: Power burden is dominated by sensing, coupling, recoupling, control, and recovery demand rather than a simple speed-to-reactor relation.
gravitic-plane.navigation: Cultivated processors reconstruct gradients, tides, shear forks, hidden terrain, and branch probabilities; independent sensory ancestry is preserved to prevent correlated biological sensor error from masquerading as confidence.
gravitic-plane.control: Local ganglia coordinate whole-vessel coupling while protecting against differential acceleration across flexible or elongated hull structures.
gravitic-plane.maintenance: Survey gravitic sensor baselines, coupling-tissue preload, structural attachments, controller latency, scar-induced phase lag, and branch-rejection pathways.
gravitic-plane.signature: Gravitational coupling and route interaction remain family-primary; biological support may add acoustic, thermal, chemical, and neural synchronization evidence.
gravitic-plane.failure: A shear fork or bad terrain solution may produce differential loading while biological faults can delay recoupling, corrupt branch voting, or create regional coupling mismatch.
gravitic-plane.infrastructure: No Ar'nock survey corridor or gravitational-terrain observatory network is confirmed.
gravitic-plane.scaling: Mass distribution and vessel span increase differential-coupling burden; capital hulls require more regional sensors and local load-aware coupling organs.
manualProcedure: prove sensor independence before accepting a branch solution
compare coupling load by hull region rather than vessel average
quarantine ganglia showing coherent-but-unverified terrain predictions
recouple only while sufficient family-specific decision horizon remains

slipstream-shear.physicalInvariant: The vessel must acquire, adhere to, forecast, and safely detach from a Q-boundary shear; an Ar'nock implementation remains a boundary-riding system, not a generic organic warp drive.
machinery: hull-distributed adhesion tissues or grown field lattice
forward Q-tomography sensory organs
sectional shear controllers linked by cultivated neural carriers
dedicated detachment and recovery organs with isolated reserve
slipstream-shear.power: Acquisition, hold, correction, sensing, computation, thermal handling, and protected detachment reserve remain separate burdens.
slipstream-shear.navigation: The control organism must forecast Q-weather, boundary curvature, wake state, exit correspondence, and adhesion margin beyond immediate detection range.
slipstream-shear.control: Sectional adhesion ganglia trim local coupling while a higher-level cultivated resolver protects whole-hull coherence and exit options.
slipstream-shear.maintenance: Inspect adhesion tissues for scar gradients, vascular starvation, local timing drift, Q-sensor contamination, and detachment-path isolation.
slipstream-shear.signature: Q-boundary and wake signatures remain family-primary; Ar'nock embodiment adds derived metabolic, thermal, biochemical, vibration, and neural activity around acquisition and recovery.
slipstream-shear.failure: Adhesion deficit, Q-weather, boundary pinch, wake resonance, or exit loss can combine with biological control latency, diseased field tissue, or exhausted regenerative reserve.
slipstream-shear.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-weather network, surveyed slipstream corridor, or wake-traffic service is confirmed.
slipstream-shear.scaling: Increasing hull area multiplies adhesion sectors and coordination latency; local autonomous ganglia become mandatory before a capital hull can remain uniformly attached.
manualProcedure: map current adhesion coverage after every hull-geometry change
validate forward Q sensing through at least two independent biological/reference chains
protect detachment reserve from route optimization
detach before local tissue or forecast uncertainty consumes the family-specific safety horizon

q-lattice.physicalInvariant: The installation must solve discrete Q address and epoch validity with complete protected-state coverage; ordinary distance and biological intuition cannot substitute for lattice adjacency.
machinery: cultivated address-resonance organs
distributed neural epoch-clock mesh
whole-vessel living state cage
state buffer and rejection/recovery organs
q-lattice.power: Energy is allocated to address lock, phase alignment, coverage, translation, exit, and protected recovery rather than a continuous thrust budget.
q-lattice.navigation: Cultivated computation maintains address hypotheses, epoch windows, alias probability, external references, and destination exclusion without averaging incompatible candidates into one confidence score.
q-lattice.control: Neural timing mesh must preserve independent clock/reference ancestry and reject regional desynchronization before commit.
q-lattice.maintenance: Recertify state-cage coverage, clock-mesh phase, resonator response, biological reference stability, and appendage/cargo inclusion after repair or growth.
q-lattice.signature: Q-state preparation/translation signatures remain primary; living resonator activity may add thermal, ionic, chemical, neural, or vibratory precursors.
q-lattice.failure: Address alias, epoch miss, coverage hole, clock split, reference poisoning, or recovery exhaustion can be triggered or worsened by scarred timing tissue, neural drift, or biological state change.
q-lattice.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-address beacon or lattice index network is confirmed.
q-lattice.scaling: The weakest local state-cage region controls validity; large hulls therefore require redundant local cage organs and clock authorities rather than stronger average coverage.
manualProcedure: enumerate every currently carried structure inside the protected-state definition
compare epoch clocks through independent reference ancestry
reject unresolved address aliases rather than selecting the biologically strongest resonance
hold recovery capacity outside discretionary translation energy

n-manifold.physicalInvariant: The system must select a higher-dimensional route while maintaining an admissible return map; biological embodiment cannot replace dimensional topology or return conditioning.
machinery: grown embedding-field structures distributed through the hull
cultivated multi-axis topology processors
independent return-map sensory and reference organs
sectional re-embedding/recovery tissues
n-manifold.power: Energy burden includes embedding, axis control, sensing/inference, route solution, return conditioning, thermal handling, and protected re-embedding capacity.
n-manifold.navigation: Neural/tissue computation infers higher-dimensional obstacles, axis state, route geometry, return-map conditioning, and ordinary-space emergence covariance.
n-manifold.control: Regional controllers maintain embedding coherence while an independent return authority is prevented from sharing a single failure ancestry with route optimization.
n-manifold.maintenance: Test axis/parity response, return-map references, embedding coverage, tomography residuals, neural topology models, and regional recovery tissue.
n-manifold.signature: Topology/embedding and emergence evidence remain family-primary; biological support produces derived state-change, metabolic, thermal, and neural signatures.
n-manifold.failure: Axis inversion, hidden obstacles, return-map divergence, topology change, or bad re-embedding can combine with cultivated-model pathology or regional biological phase drift.
n-manifold.infrastructure: No Ar'nock manifold survey network or dimensional reference infrastructure is confirmed.
n-manifold.scaling: Additional hull span and active axes increase coordination and model complexity; mature biological implementations need hierarchical local embedding control and an independently maintained return system.
manualProcedure: verify minimum sufficient active dimensionality
treat coherent unexplained tomography residuals as unresolved obstacles, not sensor noise
audit return-map evidence independently of route-optimization evidence
retain re-embedding reserve even when a shorter manifold route becomes available

fold-jump.physicalInvariant: The installation must create temporary topological adjacency between certified origin and destination volumes and obey its precommit point-of-no-return; living machinery cannot create post-commit steering authority.
machinery: grown topology-forming aperture organs
distributed protected-volume boundary tissue
cultivated endpoint/occupancy solvers
closure and ringing-recovery organs with isolated reserve
fold-jump.power: Event energy remains divided among nucleation, shaping, holding, closure/ringing control, and protected recovery.
fold-jump.navigation: Endpoint covariance, destination volume occupancy, gravity conditioning, source authentication, and topology solution bifurcation are explicitly tracked.
fold-jump.control: Neural control may continuously re-solve before commit but must hard-veto new steering claims after family-specific topology execution begins.
fold-jump.maintenance: Survey complete protected-volume anatomy, topology-former tissue, endpoint reference ancestry, closure response, and damaged flexible appendages.
fold-jump.signature: Topological transient and closure/emergence signatures remain primary; biological preparation/recovery can add chemistry, heat, vibration, and neural synchronization evidence.
fold-jump.failure: Endpoint covariance, occupancy conflict, topology bifurcation, premature commit, closure ringing, or bad gravity conditioning may combine with living coverage gaps or delayed neural rejection.
fold-jump.infrastructure: No Ar'nock fold beacon, prepared endpoint, or fold-gate infrastructure is confirmed.
fold-jump.scaling: Larger protected volumes magnify boundary certification and closure burden; living segmentation helps monitor coverage but does not relax destination-volume exclusion.
manualProcedure: prove the destination as a clear volume, not a coordinate
freeze protected-volume geometry before final topology solution
protect closure and recovery reserve
abort before commit when endpoint covariance or evidence ancestry becomes unacceptable

wormhole-gate.physicalInvariant: The installation must maintain a synchronized multiply connected throat with finite aperture, mass flux, remote-mouth state, and chronology protection; a biological gate remains infrastructure, not an enlarged ship organ by assumption.
machinery: cultivated aperture-forming ring or membrane sectors
distributed throat-stabilization tissues with structural anchoring
paired-mouth authenticated neural/reference network
industrial-scale living thermal, recovery, and isolation ecology
wormhole-gate.power: Hold, shape, synchronization, traffic, control, thermal, and protected closure/recovery loads are separately accounted.
wormhole-gate.navigation: Remote-mouth authentication and state synchronization remain independent from local prediction; stale inferred remote state cannot be reported as measured synchronization.
wormhole-gate.control: Regional living aperture sectors regulate throat geometry and mass flux under a traffic authority while chronology veto remains non-negotiable.
wormhole-gate.maintenance: Inspect anchor tissues/structures, aperture geometry, synchronization references, thermal ecology, traffic-load damage, and closure systems at both mouths.
wormhole-gate.signature: Persistent throat/topological and infrastructure signatures remain primary; living gateworks may add very large thermal, biochemical, circulatory, acoustic, and ecological signatures.
wormhole-gate.failure: Throat instability, mouth desynchronization, asymmetric mass flux, chronology trip, anchor drift, thermal saturation, or network cascade can combine with regional tissue failure or reference-organ pathology.
wormhole-gate.infrastructure: The family is inherently infrastructure-heavy, but Ar'nock ownership or construction of any gate network remains UNRESOLVED.
wormhole-gate.scaling: Aperture area, mass flux, synchronization, anchoring, service ecology, and traffic control scale independently; never model a strategic gate as a shipboard organ multiplied by size.
manualProcedure: authenticate both mouths through independent evidence
certify aperture and traffic envelope for the actual crossing geometry
reserve controlled closure capacity before admission
veto passage on chronology, synchronization, or remote-state uncertainty regardless of traffic priority

phase-displacement.physicalInvariant: The system must map a protected macroscopic state to a compatible nonlocal target while satisfying explicit engineering continuity invariants; it cannot claim to resolve metaphysical identity.
machinery: whole-object living state cage
cultivated state-mapping and target-compatibility processors
distributed continuity-reference organs with independent ancestry
post-arrival reconciliation and regenerative recovery tissues
phase-displacement.power: Preparation, reference, target lock, state mapping, reconciliation, and protected recovery are separate event burdens.
phase-displacement.navigation: The system evaluates target-state compatibility, occupancy, uncertainty, reference provenance, and engineering continuity invariants rather than a destination coordinate alone.
phase-displacement.control: Cultivated computation may certify explicit continuity tests but is prohibited from translating successful tests into a universal claim about soul, self, or metaphysical identity.
phase-displacement.maintenance: Recertify state-cage coverage, reference independence, state-media integrity, target models, reconciliation tissue, and changed biological/hull geometry.
phase-displacement.signature: State-preparation/displacement/reconciliation evidence remains family-primary; living machinery can add neural, metabolic, biochemical, thermal, and regenerative signatures.
phase-displacement.failure: Coverage hole, target alias, continuity-proof failure, reference poisoning, occupancy conflict, reconciliation divergence, or recovery exhaustion may combine with cultivated reference drift or biological configuration change.
phase-displacement.infrastructure: No Ar'nock phase-displacement beacon or target-reference infrastructure is confirmed.
phase-displacement.scaling: The minimum local state-cage and reference quality control validity; larger organisms, cargo, flexible appendages, repairs, and docked objects expand the certified state definition nonlinearly.
manualProcedure: define the exact protected object before state preparation
audit continuity-reference ancestry for independence
veto unresolved target occupancy or aliasing
perform post-arrival engineering reconciliation without claiming metaphysical proof
